- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts peak too early and then plateau or slightly decline, while true outcomes often show sharper, delayed peaks or mean-reversion after spikes.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections after high peaks; true outcomes frequently drop below forecasted levels after a spike.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of late-period corrections (last 5–10 days of 30d window), especially when true values are trending down.
- Forecast smoothness is too high; true outcomes show more volatility, particularly in mid-to-late periods.
- Model tends to ignore recent low values in history when forecasting, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Correction should be applied by reducing forecasted values by 2–5% for periods with recent high peaks or low historical volatility.
- Adjust forecast downward if true outcome shows a sharp drop after a peak, especially if model has not yet reacted to the drop.
- Use a moving average of the last 5–7 true values to adjust forecast if model is overestimating early in the window.
- Apply a “lag correction” by reducing forecast by 1–3% for each day after a peak, if true outcome shows a downward trend.
